subject.title: fix(backup): sweep stale temp artifacts before creating new backup

question: After the timestamped-output defect is fixed, should OpenClaw automatically delete stale backup temp artifacts after the grace window when no live owner is detected?
rationale: This is a destructive cleanup policy for backup artifacts; source and CI can prove scoping, but maintainer intent is needed on whether stale partial backup temps are disposable recovery/debug material.

options.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup
options.body: Land the startup sweep after the timestamped-output repair, keeping tight UUID, owner-marker, age, and directory scoping.

options.title: Require Manual Recovery Surface
options.body: Do not auto-delete backup temps until the cleanup is exposed through an explicit doctor/janitor command or user-facing recovery workflow.

options.title: Keep Manual Cleanup Only
options.body: Close or pause this path if maintainers want operators to own stale backup temp deletion outside OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Accept Guarded Cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the startup sweep after the timestamped-output repair, keeping tight UUID, owner-marker, age, and directory scoping.

likelyOwner.reason: The backup creation code was extracted into the current infra surface by this person, making them the best history-backed owner for the cleanup-policy decision.
